items.title: NEAR Intents Exploit Fully Recovered
points: Attacker exploited a vulnerability in NEAR's Intents protocol (a system that processes user transaction requests across the NEAR blockchain) and stole funds, but later returned 100% of the stolen amount.
No legal action was taken against the hacker, suggesting a voluntary return or negotiated resolution.
The incident exposed a security flaw in the Intents system.
This full recovery is rare in crypto theft cases, setting a notable industry precedent.

items.title: SEC Custody Framework Modernizes Digital Asset Regulation
points: SEC Chair Paul Atkins proposes rules permitting self-custody of crypto in certain circumstances and expanding the qualified custodian category to include state trust companies, replacing rules designed for traditional securities.
The framework removes a primary structural barrier to institutional crypto adoption by giving regulated investment advisers and funds a defined compliance path previously absent for digital assets.
Atkins called the modernization overdue for a multi-trillion-dollar asset class that has outgrown rules 'crafted for a bygone era.'

items.title: Blast Layer 2 Shuts Down
points: Blast Layer 2 (a blockchain scaling network built on top of Ethereum) is shutting down because operating costs exceeded revenue.
Users have until October 26 to withdraw funds through the standard interface.

items.title: Aave Labs Proposes Cayman Islands IP Foundation
points: Aave Labs proposes establishing a Cayman Islands IP Foundation to place its brand and intellectual property under DAO (Decentralized Autonomous Organization, a member-governed entity run via blockchain voting) governance.
Transferring assets to the foundation would require separate DAO votes.

items.title: Private x402 Launches on Aztec Testnet
points: Private x402 launches on Aztec testnet, enabling concealed agent-payment transactions via zero-knowledge proofs (cryptographic proofs that reveal information is true without disclosing the information itself) while preserving settlement flow.

items.title: Stock Tokenization Reaches Regulatory Inflection Point
points: Three legal structures now govern tokenized stocks: tokens as registered assets themselves (BlackRock BUIDL), tokens as bare-trust claims without voting rights (Coinbase stocks), and tokens as price-tracking debt securities (Robinhood Stock Tokens).

September 2026 brought concurrent milestones: SEC approved tokenized US stocks for on-chain liquidity pools, the ECB launched Pontes to bridge blockchains with central bank money, and Aave v4 went live accepting Coinbase stock tokens as collateral on Base.

Practical benefits include 24/7 trading and atomic settlement versus traditional T+1 (trades settling over one business day); BUIDL is accepted as collateral on Binance and Deribit, though most tokenized stocks exclude US persons and voting rights remain unresolved.
Dinari opened 724 US stocks to US investors in August; Robinhood's offshore stock tokens are now live in 120+ countries with plans to add in-kind redemption and voting rights.

items.title: Agentic Commerce Landscape Spans Six Sectors
points: Six sectors include consumer task-completion, AI-built businesses, enterprise process optimization, card network upgrades, crypto-native DeFi agents, and x402 pay-per-inference micropayments.

Stripe holds the largest near-term GDP impact, routing approximately 1.716% of global GDP through its protocols, while Visa and Mastercard introduce tokenized payment credentials requiring opt-in from issuing banks and merchants.
The crypto-native side shows Clawpump posting $1.5M daily volume as agents launch tokens and trade, and BlockRun's x402 marketplace spans 105 models priced $0.14/M to $10/M tokens.
Polsia, category leader for AI-built businesses, raised $30M at a $250M valuation and generated tens of thousands of companies without a breakout success, indicating early-stage development.

The recovery demonstrates rare positive outcome in crypto theft cases where stolen assets are voluntarily restored to the platform.
Intents protocol vulnerability was exploited, but the attacker's decision to return funds suggests possible ethical hacking or negotiated settlement.
